speaker: Ben Gilbert
text: Welcome back to Acquired, the podcast about great companies and the stories behind them. Today we're covering Standard Oil.

speaker: David Rosenthal
text: This is the story of how John D. Rockefeller built a company that at its peak controlled ninety percent of American oil refining.

speaker: Ben Gilbert
text: Rockefeller didn't start as a wildcatter. He started as a bookkeeper, and that discipline around costs became the whole strategy.

speaker: David Rosenthal
text: We didn't need to drill a single well to control the industry. We just needed to control the pipes and the railroads.

speaker: Ben Gilbert
text: That's the real insight here: distribution and logistics were the moat, not the oil itself. Anyone can find oil. Almost no one can move it as cheaply.

speaker: David Rosenthal
text: By 1882 the Standard Oil Trust controlled refining, transport, and marketing end to end, which is what eventually drew antitrust scrutiny.

speaker: Ben Gilbert
text: The 1911 Supreme Court breakup split it into more than thirty companies, several of which became Exxon, Chevron, and Mobil.

speaker: David Rosenthal
text: So the ending is almost funny: breaking up the monopoly made Rockefeller even richer, because the pieces were worth more separately.
